items.title: Officials Find Cascade of Problems With ICE Training in Trump’s Immigration Crackdown
items.summary: In a draft report, officials found widespread training gaps as the Department of Homeland Security sought to rapidly hire and deploy 10,000 new officers.

items.title: Stocks Skid Into a Correction, as A.I. Worries Intensify
items.summary: The S&P 500 ended the day down more than 10 percent from its recent high, in a symbolic measure of investors’ souring mood.

items.title: What Is a Stock Market Correction?
items.summary: The S&P 500 has fallen more than 10 percent from its recent high, crossing a threshold that signals investors have turned pessimistic about stocks.

items.title: How Jensen Huang Made Humiliation Routine at Nvidia
items.summary: The Nvidia co-founder’s belittling behavior toward employees goes back decades. It once led to a confidential settlement agreement with an executive who said Mr. Huang “terrorized” staff.

items.title: Nvidia Said to Face S.E.C. Probe Into Its Accounting Practices
items.summary: Questions around the company’s accounting had surfaced amid revelations about its questionable chip sales in Asia.

items.title: Jury in Palisades Fire Trial Finds Man Guilty of Arson in Devastating Blaze
items.summary: The defendant, Jonathan Rinderknecht, was found guilty on two counts. The verdict provides a measure of accountability for a painful chapter in recent L.A. history.

items.title: Trump Administration Says Army Can Blow Up Lead-Laced Explosives
items.summary: The detonation, now set for Monday, could create a cloud of lead dust stretching for miles over homes and farms, the Army has said. Environmental groups are seeking an emergency stay.

items.title: Anthropic Mathematician Claims to Solve Riemann Hypothesis With Help From Claude
items.summary: If confirmed, the proof of the Riemann hypothesis would cement the field’s sense that no unsolved problem is safe from artificial intelligence.

items.title: Playing ‘Key of Life,’ Stevie Wonder Invites All to Match His Joy
items.summary: Wonder’s optimism was refracted around Madison Square Garden as he performed his “Songs in the Key of Life” album on a 50th anniversary tour.

items.title: Judge Approves $7 Billion Settlement Over Claims That Roundup Caused Cancer
items.summary: The ruling, in a nationwide class-action suit, is expected to end tens of thousands of lawsuits by people claiming that Roundup caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

items.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
items.summary: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.

items.title: The latest from Trump's press conference
items.summary: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

items.title: Rising seas have forced this Quinault village to relocate
items.summary: The Quinault Indian Nation has moved its largest village away from rising seas and tsunamis

items.title: Trump's impact on an Ohio steel plant
items.summary: The giant steel plant in Middletown, Ohio planned to switch away from using coke, a refined form of coal. The switch would have cut hazardous air pollution -- and greenhouse gas emissions. But that plan has changed under…

items.title: MLK's handwritten draft of iconic speech on display for the first time
items.summary: The only known handwritten draft of The Reverend Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech is on display in his hometown. The iconic phrase, however, never made it on the page.

items.title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
items.summary: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.

items.title: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
items.summary: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.

items.title: How Orchestra Noir turned classical music into a cultural movement
items.summary: Orchestra Noir is back on tour, selling out stages across the country and proving classical music can be anything you want it to be.

items.title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers little results
items.summary: At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.

items.title: Texas execution took over an hour as staff struggled to find vein; Reinaldo Dennes moaned about pain
items.summary: The same day Dennes was given lethal injection, Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year.

items.title: Pandemic-era law passed unconstitutionally because of proxy voting, appeals court rules
items.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit upheld Texas’s injunction stopping accommodations for pregnant workers by targeting how Congress passed a massive Biden-era funding bill.

items.title: L.A. train heists net thieves more than $22 million in goods, feds say
items.summary: A Southern California crew is charged with breaking into more than 70 shipping containers in 31 months, stealing more than $22 million in shoes and other goods.

items.title: Federal health panel reshaped by RFK Jr. faces political interference concerns
items.summary: Some members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force expressed concerns that the changes from the Trump administration could make the group less reliable and more open to conflicts of interest.

items.title: U.S. stocks slump into correction territory amid tech and AI worries
items.summary: Markets on Friday posted their worst week since worries about President Donald Trump’s tariffs caused a global sell-off in April 2025.

items.title: Texas governor-elect and Trump agree to work together on border security
items.summary: President Donald Trump says he had a “very productive call” with Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, who characterized it as “a very positive conversation.”

items.title: Hat had traveled too far into Fiona’s intestines to safely remove, zoo says
items.summary: There was no way to use endoscopy to reach the hat that the beloved hippo ingested, Cincinnati Zoo officials said, and laparoscopic surgery was not possible.

items.title: Child begged for life in 911 call as father killed family, sheriff says
items.summary: The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office said authorities are investigating the killing of four people.

items.title: Stefanik family’s D.C. home sells to mystery buyer for $900K over list price
items.summary: After not selling at a lower price and eventually being taken off the market, the home of the outgoing congresswoman from New York sold in June for $2.9 million.

items.title: Jonathan Yardley, Pulitzer-winning book critic at The Post, dies at 87
items.summary: For 33 years, he helped Washington Post readers find the next good book. His reviews could be prickly or inspiring, and pushed some authors — including Michael Chabon — to new heights.

items.title: Mamdani proposes five-year extension to shutter notorious Rikers Island prison
items.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s plan moves the deadline from 2027 to 2032 to allow time to build the borough-based jails slated to replace Rikers.
